channel.title: SquirrelJME
channel.description: SquirrelJME is a Java ME 8 Virtual Machine.

item.title: SquirrelJME has a Codeberg Mirror!
item.description: SquirrelJME is now also on Codeberg at the following URL: https://codeberg.org/SquirrelJME/SquirrelJME! Like the other Git mirrors, this is a direct conversion of the Fossil repository which is then directly pushed to the remote.

item.title: The New Year
item.description: The next year is very much upon us, I am hopeful that for SquirrelJME's tenth year that SquirrelJME 0.4.0 is released at some point in 2026. However, in the meantime there have been a number of changes and updates which have occured.

item.title: Dropping Flatpak Support
item.description:
SquirrelJME will no longer be building Flatpaks, keeping them up to date, nor showing them on the download page. The build process for Flatpaks is just too limiting and the experience as a whole is just a pain.
For existing Flatpak users, it is recommended that you switch to either the _Standalone_ or _Install4J_ installer version.

item.title: Development Is Resuming
item.description:
My father passed away in late July which has made for a difficult August, along with getting the flu for a few weeks as well which definitely did not help. So for the lack of updates and such for both months, is due to these two reasons. Thank you for understanding.
Early July I have merged in NanoCoat's code execution which is a major chunk of the virtual machine and is a major milestone. Just before my father passed away, I started work on implementing the stack cached interpreter which is a science heavy and very theoretical piece of code that would effectively be a major performance increase for NanoCoat. Stack caching is pretty important as it takes care of about 90% of the performance gains, so once this is done then NanoCoat should be executing quite quickly.
For now though as I work on that in the background, I will continue the code execution bits and work on getting NanoCoat functional and operational first. It will run, but it will not be the most optimal performance wise. It will still be faster than SpringCoat since it is running in native code and does not need to have the JVM's JIT compiler to compile the interpreter.
Other than that, there is not much else to update!

item.title: DoJa audio support has been merged in!
item.description:
Back in May, _Guy Perfect_ kindly wrote and donated an MA-3 music emulator for DoJa! This has now been merged in! This is supported for both Windows and Linux. For Linux you will need Open Source System support, either natively, with ALSA emulation (`snd_pcm_oss` and `alsa-oss`), or with the PulseAudio/PipeWire daemon `osspd`.
Do note that if audio is playing for DoJa in _SpringCoat_ the performance will be very sluggish as there is no acceleration support currently, you will have to run the _Hosted_ version.
There may be some audio issues on Windows as that is not my main development system.

item.title: SquirrelJME and FreeJ2ME-Plus can share saves!
item.description:
In cooperation with the developer of FreeJ2ME-Plus, a derivation of SquirrelJME's existing save format was created which now both emulators implement which means that saves are sharable between the two emulators!
The format consists of a JSON metadata file along with basic binaries of record data, so it is very simple and easy to implement.
A specification is available at https://squirreljme.cc/doc/trunk/assets/doc/save-format.mkd.

item.title: There is now an installer!
item.description: An installer for Windows, Linux, and macOS is now available! There additionally is update functionality, which should work. It should now be easier to use the standalone version without having to install a Java SE virtual machine yourself and using the command line, unless you still wish to.

item.title: Belated April and May Update!
item.description:
Okay, so I kind of forgot to post an update last month! Oops, I knew I was forgetting something!
In May there was a kindly contributed MA-3 music emulator donated to SquirrelJME by the alias of _Guy Perfect_, which means that SquirrelJME will soon get sound support for both MIDP and DoJa! I am currently working on integrating this taking a break from NanoCoat's execution work to get this into the standalone! Will definitely have an update once that is in!
There were some important compatibility improvements in April, which will definitely improve things! SquirrelJME now changes the functionality of certain API functions depending on the platform version requested by the software. There have been changes over the course of both Java ME and DoJa where the behavior of methods just changed! Now this is correctly handled and as such, graphically everything looks far better and less glitchy!
The other major compatibility improvement is that the Record Management System, or RMS, now is implemented in a proper way and is stored to disk. So any data or progress that an application/game saves will be stored and resumes. This also applies to DoJa as well!
There were additional minor compatibility fixes with DoJa due to some software requiring very lenient scratchpad behavior, as such this has been additionally applied to SquirrelJME. This mostly fixes the Legacy of Network and Phantom of Network games.
The number pad now properly works and inverts accordingly so that it matches the layout of the dial-pad, since keyboard number pads have the calculator layout.
Work on NanoCoat code execution continues, not much to say there!

item.title: March Update!
item.description:
SquirrelJME now has a single standalone Jar which is multi-platform, so now it will be easier to run it without having to fully know what your system is.
I decided to just merge in the calendar implementation despite it being incomplete, since it was a very long-lived branch that I just wanted to close. A large number of DoJa software requires a calendar implementation, so this should be an initial first-step for that.
Other than that, there has been continued work on NanoCoat which is progressing well. Currently, I am working on the main startup sequence for applications.

item.title: February Update
item.description: Hi! This month was pretty productive! There were a few bug fixes around buffers, and DataInputStream.readUTF() being completely incorrect... oops! One of the major things is the forced serialization of ScritchUI pencil drawing operations, which fixes a large number of graphical glitches, freezes, and crashes due to changes in how modern hardware works. Other than that, I have been progressing rather nicely with NanoCoat which has been very nice.

item.title: SpringCoat Performance Improvements
item.description: I have not done much this month as my break continues, however I have been slowly getting back into the flow of things. There have been major improvements to SpringCoat performance around strings and DoJa application start times have been reduced greatly if you are using standalone. On the otherwise for NanoCoat, work continues on code execution!

item.title: Quite a year!
item.description: This year has been quite the year! In the current month of December I have mostly been making minor bug fixes and other small improvements around many miscellaneous areas, along with working on the macOS Cocoa UI.

item.title: An Anti-Burnout Break is Needed
item.description: The year has been exciting and so much has been done, but I also recognize that I need a much-needed break.
